GameDBLocalizedString.Text: Generates<color=SOTS_COLOR_GOLD> 1000</color> additional <color=SOTS_COLOR_GOLD>Aura coins</color> per turn and further increases unit production.
Shared safe storage accessible from any base with this building.
Adds one more commander for hire. You can rehire your last retreated commander for an unlimited amount of time.
Allows you to build Goo Spitters for your armies.
You cay bury BIO units here. They will get reborn as Fungors.
Ancient Primals left behind all sorts of ruins. Some damaged monuments are beyond repair, but in some places, there is still a spark of life waiting to be awakened and provide the power to the base.

Crystalization tech. The backbone of Primal science is not easy to repair. But some damage is mendable (or rather, jerry-rigged) by the biomass of the base. The stronger the base, the better it can compensate for the damage.

What was once broken never recovers to its former self. There will always be a scar. Although corrupted and deformed, the Primal reactor is functioning nonetheless. The fact that it's running without doomsday consequences is a minor miracle, unachievable by the technology of any other faction.

After the Holy War tore the flesh from Primal cities asunder, only their crystal skeletons remained. But these were no ordinary remains. The crystal technology of the Primals was designed to last and when you take into account their ability of self repair, "last" is meant literally.

A space within another space. Sort of a utopic fridge through which you can reach your beers from anywhere ... I wonder why this wonderful technology did not change the world or break the story like "eagles bearing the ring to Mordor"? Please don't ask me any more.
More than anything, it resembles digestion, but can extract precious compounds from ... literally anything. And they say you're good for nothing. Jump in and prove them wrong.

Once, distance was not a problem, but today, traveling through Primal teleports is risky business. A hundred years from now, a successful transport will be a rarity, and in three hundred, a legend. So, all factions must come up with their own designs or prepare for some really worn-out soles.

The Outworlders are strong and resilient, but they lack the basic skills for survival in the harsh conditions of the Siren System. They are making mistake after mistake, and Tumori chieftains are always there to capitalize on those mistakes.

Since the last crusade was lost in the swamps of planet Chimera, the tribes thrived. Then, the Outworlders came, and the hunt began anew. Hard times breed strong chieftains—those who have taken war names and reside in the host breed for combat.

What happens to the swarm if its size shrinks to a point that it can barely control the host or even hold consciousness? Not everyone is honored with the opportunity to merge with the Ancestorial Swarm—only those renowned for their sharp skills and deep knowledge. For the rest, there are "simpler" tasks.

Assemblers were true marvels of Primal technology. Essentially giant 3D printers. It is no wonder Tumori put in tremendous effort to get them up and running. Even if they operate at only 0.5% of their former capacity, they're still one of the greatest assets of each Tumori base.

Not all Outworlders are hostile. For example, the Rogue Traffickers were the first who stretched their hand towards ... ok, towards Tumori "pockets" but, to their own amazement, discovered that if you watch your manners, a friendship with tribesmen could be quite beneficial.

Baloos can multiply like rabbits on an Aussie farm, but Ascon's crystal growth process takes time ... until its size crosses a certain point, when the growth will dramatically accelerate. So, EAT AND BREED, you damn teddy bears! The tribe needs new hosts! We are at war, goddamit!

When death knocks at the gate, and consciousness begins slipping from the swarm's grasp, there is time to move on and join one of the Ancestral Swarms. All the knowledge of the tribe's previous generations is preserved and ready to be passed on to those who seek it.

The Tumori can instantly learn complex skills and knowledge coded in the memory tissue, delivered by individuals between swarms. Yeah, baby, like in the Matrix! Though directed by David Cronenberg. But you can still say "I know kung fu" in the end, so does it really matter?

Each swarm consists of many types of specialised individuals. The variance depends on the swarm's current requirements. The Ancestral Swarm stores knowledge; therefore, there is barely any space for anything other than memory-bearing individuals. In short: big brain, no sense of humor.

It's no small burden inheriting a world from a civilization so advanced that your fanciest tech is like a baking soda volcano next to a nuclear submarine. Yet, Tumori are no quitters. They are always on the hunt for another lost dig site to deepen their understanding of Primal technology.

Almost all Outworlders are aggressive aliens and do not wish for peaceful coexistence. BUT! They have technology. Although it lacks the grace natural to biological structures, it is pretty useful, therefore worth stealing.
Biotechnology is the pride and joy of all Tumori. In their hands, it can actually jerry-rig some of the ancient Primal machines. All other factions must be green with envy over this!

Tumori tribesmen have always been hungry for the mind-influencing "magic" manifested by Primal artifacts. Eventually, the Shamans studying their strange effects were able to decipher and simplify some of the principles enough to mimic them.

The Tumori have inherited some mighty, old-world weaponry. Technology so advanced it gets mistaken for magic. It's only thanks to these "magic weapons" that they were able to survive the genocidal crusades launched by the Children of the Source.

Some of the "magic weapons" inherited from the Primals were lost in wars, and some lost their abilities due to aging without proper maintenance. As they approached modern times, the Tumori have increasingly had to rely on their own inferior technology.

You don't need to understand the technology to use it, and that's doubly true when it comes to weapons. At first, the Rogue Traffickers were reluctant to deal with arms, but when they learned that the Tumori paid in Primal artifacts, they overcame their moral dilemma with surprising ease.

There is no way to reprogram these cheap UNSS turrets to recognize the wide variety of hosts used by the Tumori. Instead, turrets are operated by swarms so old that they can barely hold consciousness. There are incidents, yes, but it's way better than all other options.

The carnivorous Fugor mycelia are not "picky"; any living tissue will suffice. At first, it's not pretty nor silent, but as the digestion progresses, movement becomes scarce, and noises get suppressed.

Young swarms compulsively seek their first host even before they form a consciousness. The Fungor mycelia produce attractants to help them find their first home. Still, it's less moldy than the first place I could rent. Nah, I am joking, I am ... please, give me a moment.

As the swarm grows, it develops its consciousness, but without knowledge, it is still "hollow". Then, an older swarm sends its individuals packed with memory tissue ... and that's it. Congratulations, you have reached maturity!

They cannot simply say, "Just catch a little Baloo and inoculate it with the crystal necessary for shooting beams of energy." No! There is the Ceremony of Conjunction, the Ritual of a Thousand Eyes, etc, till everyone is in the state of absolute higgledy-piggledy.

The bigger the head, the bigger the crystal. The bigger the crystal, the stronger the beam ... till the moment the crystal outgrows the head and kills the host. Fortunately for the swarm, it means just a change of host. Being a parasite has its advantages.

The UNSS Research Division figured out how to copy the metamorphosis mechanism. The only thing holding them back is the exponential growth of energy consumption whenever they want to prolong their Mimicking Tactics beyond a certain point. Surprise surprise, nature vs lab, 1:0.

Living tissue can't mimic all the properties of a reinforced steel plate. No matter what molecular-bullshit, sci-fi somersault you make, you will always land on your head. So, choose wisely when deciding what to turn into next, my mighty morphing friend!

If you're struggling to put down a formidable enemy, aim for the head! But even a headshot will not save you against this creature with a dispersed nervous system and several independent ganglia centers ready to take over the "wheel". The Slugtor is the perfect bullet sponge.

Slimy and squishy is a pretty precise description, with one exception. Under the Slugtor's soft skin lies a layer of interlinked zirconium dioxide scales, giving the beast the toughness of a Special Forces guy from an '80s action flick.
Yeah, teleportation is a great idea until you take a trip with, I don't know, for example, a fly in your pocket! "Something Went Wrong, Seth! When You Went Through, Something Went Wrong!"

During the first days of exploration, Michael Moore 3C and his troops encountered a Malarion. "Pardon my language," said the Hesperidian, "the incidence of such a huge fly gives us all the information about the depth of sh*t we are currently stepping in. Gents, on the count of three, we run to the landing module. THREE!"

People speculated that Skull Collectors were just horribly mutated humans. Then the UNSS released a dismissive disclaimer by a man in a white cloak, which calmed the crowds. I was calm too until I noticed the "hand-wash-only" icon on one of their loincloths.

Long-distance teleportation is a pain in the ... is a problem. You'd think that making only short jumps would be much safer until coming across a dead Skull Hunter whose lower half ended in a tree. It all stands and falls with reasonable distance estimation.

The oldest genetic matrices that enabled the revival of this beast date back to Primal times. But how exactly Primal society benefited from the presence of these carnivorous monsters is quite hard to imagine.

Every tribe accumulated a different collection of knowledge in its memory heritage, but there are names known to each Tumori, regardless of their tribe: Swift Argionar, mighty Ren-Tear, unbeaten Devour, dreadful Undying, ... names of the great Raughirs of old.
